figures.label: Figure 1
figures.caption: Overview of SUPRA-Tex. Left: image-to-material translation. A 2D material translator estimates lighting-separated albedo, metallic, and roughness maps from a single reference image. Middle: native observation encoding. Using the mesh $\mathcal{M}$ and camera projection $\pi$, we project valid predictions onto visible surface voxels and omit unobserved voxels from the partial PBR input. The frozen material encoder $E_{\mathrm{mat}}$ maps these partial PBR attributes into the generation target’s latent space. These latents, together with coverage and boundary metadata, form the observation representation $\mathcal{C}_{o}$. Right: observation-guided completion. Conditioned on geometry latents $G$, the interleaved flow transformer generates complete material latents $Z_{0}$ from noise $Z_{1}$. In the inset, the fixed, read-only stream $O$ supplies keys and values, while the generation stream $X$ alternates updates over cells without observations ($\mathcal{U}$) and the full surface ($\mathcal{S}$). The frozen decoder $D_{\mathrm{mat}}$ converts $Z_{0}$ into surface PBR materials, lit from the left and right.
figures.headline: Diagram shows reference-view PBR maps are projected onto visible voxels, encoded, and used as conditions for generating complete material latents.

figures.caption: Limitations under imperfect inputs and incomplete observations. (a) The front output exhibits local motif distortion around the dragon head; the oblique view reveals a spurious protrusion in the underlying geometry. (b) Two front-oblique views show spurious protrusions in the upstream geometry that remain visible after texture refinement. (c) The glossy painted-wood appearance is assigned a high metallic value. The front output in (a) and both outputs in (d) use unlit base color; the oblique output in (a) and both outputs in (b) use PBR rendering under the same neutral lighting.

figures.label: Figure 6
figures.caption: Interleaved flow transformer. One forward pass through 60 distinct blocks arranged in 30 alternating pairs. The fixed observation stream $O$ (orange) supplies keys and values without queries or state updates. The generation stream $X$ spans the full active latent-cell set $\mathcal{S}$, with states at observed cells $\mathcal{S}_{o}$ (purple) and cells without any observation $\mathcal{U}=\mathcal{S}\setminus\mathcal{S}_{o}$ (teal); the subscript $o$ denotes observed. An observed cell may still contain unseen surface voxels. Even-indexed blocks query and update $X_{\mathcal{U}}$; odd-indexed blocks query and update all of $X$. Both block types read keys and values from all of $O$ and $X$, and the output projection predicts velocities over all $N=|\mathcal{S}|$ cells. Source labels denote tokens before normalization, time modulation, and attention projections. At inference, 25 Euler sampling steps each invoke a full transformer forward pass.
figures.headline: Interleaved blocks update unobserved cells in even-indexed layers and all cells in odd-indexed layers while observation tokens stay read-only.
citing_sentences: Figure 6 in Appendix A.2 illustrates the update schedule.

abstract: Single image 3D generation aims to dress a given 3D mesh with relightable materials while faithfully preserving the visual details of a reference image. Existing methods either introduce artifacts when fusing inconsistent multi-view predictions or struggle to preserve fine details through implicit image-feature conditioning. To resolve these challenges, we introduce SUPRA-Tex, built on the principle of decoupling visible-material estimation, surface alignment, and observation-guided 3D completion. This division of labor allows the 3D generator, trained on limited 3D data, to focus its capacity on preserving visible evidence and completing unobserved surfaces. Specifically, we first train an MLLM-based image editing model to predict lighting-separated PBR maps in the reference view. We then project these maps onto the visible surface and encode them with the pretrained material VAE encoder into native observation latents that share the generation target's latent space. An interleaved flow transformer holds these latents as fixed, read-only anchors while alternating unobserved-region and full-surface updates to generate complete material latents. This design achieves super-alignment with the reference, delivering What You See Is What You Get fidelity on visible regions and coherent completion on unobserved surfaces. Trained solely on public datasets, SUPRA-Tex achieves SOTA performance in both geometry-conditioned texturing and end-to-end asset generation, matching or even exceeding leading commercial systems on in-the-wild images. Project page: https://supra-3d.github.io/supratex/

sections.body: The paper targets relightable 3D assets from one reference image, which requires super-alignment: fine text, logos and patterns must sit at their visible surface locations, and unobserved regions must be completed consistently. Multi-view pipelines fuse predictions that disagree across views, which can cause seams, ghosting and blurred details. Native 3D generators avoid view fusion but must infer PBR properties, place reference details and synthesize unseen materials at once. SUPRA-Tex separates these tasks: a 2D model estimates visible materials, projection aligns them to the surface, and a 3D generator completes the rest. The stated contributions are native observation encoding and an interleaved flow transformer that uses fixed, read-only observation anchors.
sections.heading: 1 Introduction
sections.headline: Multi-view fusion and native 3D generation both lose fine reference details, motivating a split into material estimation, alignment and completion.

sections.body: Multi-view texturing methods synthesize views in 2D, then project and blend them onto the mesh, which can blur or ghost sharp reference details. Optimization-based methods distill diffusion priors into PBR maps. Native texture generators work on point, octree, UV or latent representations, and some add partial observations or spatially aligned image features. The section states that even with spatially aligned image features, the 3D generator must still infer materials, preserve reference details and complete unobserved surfaces. SUPRA-Tex instead completes materials in native 3D space and uses projected observations as conditioning anchors rather than fusing synthesized views into the final texture.
sections.heading: 2 Related Work
sections.headline: Prior texturing either fuses inconsistent multi-view predictions or conditions a native generator on implicit image features.

sections.body: The method has three stages. First, an MLLM-based image editing model predicts albedo and metallic-roughness maps from the photograph in a single forward pass at the fixed maximum-noise endpoint, which takes 1.2 s on one H800. Second, the predictions are projected onto visible surface voxels, filtered by foreground-mask erosion and depth-discontinuity checks, and encoded by the frozen material encoder into observation latents. Each latent cell also carries a coverage value and a graph-step boundary distance. Third, an interleaved flow transformer conditions on geometry latents and fixed observation anchors while generating complete material latents, which the frozen decoder converts into surface PBR materials.
sections.heading: 3 Method
sections.headline: SUPRA-Tex estimates reference-view PBR maps, encodes them as fixed observation anchors, and completes the full-surface material latents.

sections.body: Given-geometry texturing uses the ground-truth mesh and a forward-lit reference image, with renders at the reference view and 15 additional views on DTC-Tex and Complex-Tex. Table 1 compares ten baselines. Against feature-conditioned Pixal3D⋆, shaded PSNR improves by 1.7 dB and 1.2 dB, and albedo PSNRfg improves by 2.0 dB and 0.9 dB, on DTC-Tex and Complex-Tex respectively. LumiTex trails by more than 2 dB in shaded PSNR and by over 1.5 dB in albedo PSNR on both datasets. Table 6 reports sampling times of 8.440 s for SUPRA-Tex and 10.103 s for joint-update attention on DTC-Tex, a speedup of 1.20×. These runtime measurements compare separate checkpoints and do not isolate interleaving alone.
sections.heading: 4 Experiments
sections.headline: SUPRA-Tex leads all shaded and PBR metrics in given-geometry texturing on both evaluation datasets.

sections.body: The section lists four limits. Large image-geometry discrepancies can place projected observations on incorrect surface locations, and the geometry stays fixed during material generation. Upstream generators can add implausible unseen structures that the texture model cannot remove. Text or patterns that continue past the visible region can be completed inconsistently across the visibility boundary. The 2D estimator can misassign properties, for example a high metallic value on a non-metallic surface, and the 3D generator may retain that error. The cases are qualitative, with no corrected-geometry controls, no measured unseen-surface ground truth, and no paired two-view result.
sections.heading: 5 Limitations
sections.headline: Errors in upstream geometry, 2D material estimates and unobserved regions limit fidelity and asset quality.

sections.body: The conclusion restates the design: visible-material estimation and surface alignment are separated from 3D generation, and native observation latents serve as fixed, read-only anchors. The authors report top results among the evaluated methods for geometry-conditioned texturing and end-to-end asset generation, with training on public data only. With synthetic back-view conditioning, the method is competitive with commercial systems in human evaluations on a mixed real-and-synthetic comparison set. The section concludes that spatially aligned, directly usable material observations reconcile reference fidelity with full-surface generation.
sections.heading: 6 Conclusion
sections.headline: Trained only on public data, SUPRA-Tex reaches top results among evaluated methods and is competitive with commercial systems.

sections.body: The appendix gives method details, including the interleaved transformer's token dimensions and update schedule. It covers training data, the 2D material estimator's adaptation and training, and 3D generator optimization with checkpoint selection. Evaluation protocols include dataset construction, rendering cameras, alignment, metrics, baseline configurations and commercial comparisons. Further sections report 2D material prediction accuracy, ablation settings, the partial-versus-complete encoding diagnostic, and observed-support encoding compared with zero filling. The remaining sections contain extra qualitative comparisons, texture editing with synthetic back-view conditions, and a symbol table with dimensions.
sections.heading: Appendix
sections.headline: The appendix gives training data, optimization, evaluation protocols, ablations, extra qualitative comparisons and a notation table.
